title: [Column] In Search of More Free Time (Three-Day Weekends)

blocks.source: 【コラム】自由な時間を求めて（週休三日）
blocks.translation: [Column] In Search of More Free Time (Three-Day Weekends)

blocks.source: 今日はちょっと趣向を変えて、仕事の話をしてみます。直接関係はありませんが、これも一応創作活動に関わる大事な部分です。
blocks.translation: Today, I’d like to change things up a little and talk about work. It isn’t directly related, but it is still an important part of my creative activities.

blocks.source: 何といっても、創作に専念するには、時間の確保が必須だからです。
blocks.translation: After all, securing time is essential if you want to devote yourself to creative work.

blocks.source: 毎日７時に起きて出社、帰宅するのは２２時過ぎ――みたいな生活をしていては、時間を作るのは、困難でしょう。これは趣味が生きがいの社会人にとって死活問題でもあります。
blocks.translation: If you live a life where you get up at 7:00 every day, go to work, and don’t get home until after 22:00, it would be difficult to make time. This is also a matter of life and death for working people whose hobbies are their reason for living.

blocks.source: 酷くなれば、「生きるために働いている」のか「働くために生きている」のか、分からなくなってきます。こうなればまさに社畜の完成です。
blocks.translation: When things get really bad, you start to lose track of whether you’re “working to live” or “living to work.” At that point, you have truly become a corporate slave.

blocks.source: そしてそこで「お金を稼ぐのが大変なのは当然だ」「人生なんてそんなものだ」と諦めるのは簡単です。
blocks.translation: It is easy to give up at that point, thinking, “Of course, making money is difficult,” or “That’s just how life is.”

blocks.source: けれど、そこで終わっていては始まりません。真にやりたいことがあるのなら、工夫をして時間を作るところから勝負というわけです。
blocks.translation: But if you stop there, nothing will ever begin. If there is something you truly want to do, the real challenge starts with finding ways to make time for it.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、僕も日々時間を確保するために戦っています。
blocks.translation: That’s why I, too, fight every day to secure time for myself.

blocks.source: 具体的には週休三日で就職してみました。大の男がやることでないのは承知の上ですが、一度やってみたかったのです。
blocks.translation: Specifically, I tried finding a job with three days off per week. I knew it wasn’t something a grown man should do, but I had wanted to try it at least once.

blocks.source: 仕事内容はプログラマです。「週休三日となれば、安めのバイトしかないのかな？」と漠然と考えていましたが、派遣会社に駄目元で頼んでみたら、わりとあっさり見つけてきてくれました。
blocks.translation: I work as a programmer. I vaguely assumed that “if I wanted three days off per week, I’d probably have to settle for a low-paying part-time job,” but when I asked a temp agency as a last resort, they found me a position surprisingly easily.

blocks.source: 給与水準も特に問題なく、フルタイム時代と大差ありません。少なくとも、ＩＴ業界については柔軟な会社も多いようです。
blocks.translation: The pay was not a problem either, and it was not much different from when I worked full-time. At least in the IT industry, there seem to be many flexible companies.

blocks.source: 「短時間労働でまともな給料を得られるのは欧米の話であって、日本では無理」
blocks.translation: "Being able to earn a decent salary while working short hours is something you hear about in Europe and the United States, but it’s impossible in Japan."

blocks.source: というのは、働く側の固定観念も大きいかもしれませんね。
blocks.translation: That may also be largely an assumption held by workers themselves.

blocks.source: ところで、「週休三日で生活できるのか？」と疑問に思われたかもしれませんが、わりと余裕です。
blocks.translation: By the way, you may be wondering, “Can you really live with three days off per week?” Surprisingly, it’s quite comfortable.

blocks.source: 僕の場合、独身貴族の上に、ＰＣとネットと僅かな費用があれば完結できる趣味がほとんど。浪費とは全くの無縁。普通にやっていれば、手取りの大半が貯金に回るレベルです。
blocks.translation: In my case, I am a lifelong bachelor, and most of my hobbies can be enjoyed with nothing more than a PC, an internet connection, and a small amount of money. I have absolutely no connection with wasteful spending. If I live normally, I save most of my take-home pay.

blocks.source: さらには、その貯金を運用すれば、働かなくとも多少の収入を得ることもできるというわけです。不労所得バンザイ。
blocks.translation: Furthermore, by investing those savings, I can earn a little income even without working. Long live passive income.

blocks.source: そうして、
blocks.translation: And so,

blocks.source: ・正社員
blocks.translation: ・Full-time employee

blocks.source: ・派遣社員（フルタイム）
blocks.translation: ・Temporary employee (full-time)

blocks.source: ・派遣社員（週休三日） ←今ここ
blocks.translation: ・Temporary employee (three days off per week) ←Current position

blocks.source: ・早期リタイアしてニート ←最終目標
blocks.translation: ・Retire early and become a NEET ←Ultimate goal

blocks.source: という感じで順調（？）にステップダウンしています。だんだん社会のレールから外れている気がしますが、これも自分で決めたこと。会社にずっと勤めねばならないなんて、強迫観念を捨てて楽になりました。今は適度に仕事を辞めて、失業保険でバカンスを取れるのが最高です。
blocks.translation: I have been steadily (?) stepping down the ladder like this. I feel like I am gradually falling off society’s prescribed path, but this is something I decided for myself. I feel much more at ease after letting go of the notion that I have to keep working for the same company forever. These days, the best thing is being able to quit my job at reasonable intervals and take vacations funded by unemployment benefits.

blocks.source: というわけで念願の週休三日
blocks.translation: And so, my long-awaited three days off per week

blocks.source: ――だったのですが、落とし穴がありました。
blocks.translation: —or so I thought, but there was a catch.

blocks.source: はい。実際に入った会社が少しばかりブラックな職場だったのです。
blocks.translation: Yes. As it turned out, the company I joined was a somewhat toxic workplace.

blocks.source: 社内の雰囲気が暗く重苦しい。仕事中から昼休みまで一切の私語が皆無。
blocks.translation: The atmosphere in the office was gloomy and oppressive. There was absolutely no idle conversation, from working hours through lunch breaks.

blocks.source: 従業員のほとんどが小声。わずか２ｍ離れた人の声が聞き取れない。もしかして、元気がない人を選んで採用しているのだろうかと疑うレベル。
blocks.translation: Almost all the employees spoke in low voices. I couldn’t hear someone speaking just two meters away. It was enough to make me wonder whether they deliberately hired people who lacked energy.

blocks.source: リーダーが恐ろしく無愛想・高圧的。この人も小声なので、何度も聞き返さないと会話が成り立たない。上２つは我慢できても、これだけは無理だった。
blocks.translation: The leader was frighteningly unfriendly and overbearing. This person also spoke in a low voice, so it was impossible to have a conversation without repeatedly asking them to repeat themselves. I could put up with the first two things, but this was impossible.

blocks.source: 納得の時給がもらえて、週休三日。サービス残業はおろか、残業もほとんどありません。それだけ聞けば、どうみたってホワイトです。
blocks.translation: I was paid an acceptable hourly wage and had three days off per week. There was almost no overtime, let alone unpaid overtime. If you only heard those details, it would obviously seem like a perfectly good workplace.

blocks.source: しかしながら、そんな利点を全て吹き飛ばす程の居心地の悪さ。この会社、今まで勤めてきた職場とは次元が違う――と初日に直感できるレベルでした。
blocks.translation: However, the discomfort was enough to wipe out all those advantages. From the very first day, I could tell instinctively that this company was on an entirely different level from every workplace I had worked at before.

blocks.source: なんだかんだ言って、今までの職場はまともだったんだなあ――ということを嫌というほど思い知ったわけです。いくら時間があっても、精神力が削がれる職場では本末転倒。創作にはやはり精神的な余裕もないといけません。
blocks.translation: I was forced to realize, more than I ever wanted to, that my previous workplaces had actually been perfectly normal. No matter how much free time you have, working somewhere that drains your mental energy defeats the whole purpose. Creative work also requires a certain amount of mental breathing room.

blocks.source: もちろん、退職（契約終了）の旨をこちらから伝えました。今月末には脱出できる見込みです。
blocks.translation: Naturally, I informed them that I would be resigning (ending my contract). I expect to escape by the end of this month.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、僕の週休三日計画の船出はあえなく失敗しました。
blocks.translation: And so, the launch of my three-day-weekend plan ended in failure.

blocks.source: とはいえ、これで諦めるつもりはありません。週休三日だろうが二日だろうが、ブラックな会社はブラックという当たり前のことを痛感しただけです。
blocks.translation: That said, I have no intention of giving up over this. I have simply been reminded of the obvious fact that a toxic company is a toxic company, whether you have three days off per week or two.

blocks.source: 幸い、週休三～四日の案件は他にもあるそうなので、再度チャレンジしたいと思います。次はまともな会社であることを願いながら……。
blocks.translation: Fortunately, I hear there are other positions offering three to four days off per week, so I would like to try again. I just hope the next one is a decent company…

blocks.source: 今回はちょっと生々しいことを交えてみましたがどうでしょう？ ある意味では時間の確保こそ創作における最大の壁なので、あえて身も蓋もなく書いてみました。
blocks.translation: I included some rather raw details this time—what do you think? In a sense, securing time is the greatest obstacle to creative work, so I deliberately wrote about it without sugarcoating anything.

blocks.source: 「社会人＝懲役四十年」なんて酷い自虐もありますが、そうネガティブにならず、色々と考えてみれば抜け道はあるように思います。
blocks.translation: There is some harsh self-deprecation along the lines of “being a working adult means forty years in prison,” but if you avoid becoming so negative and think things through, it seems there may be ways out.

blocks.source: というか創作とか関係なく、「生活より仕事を優先するような本末転倒な社会は、そろそろ終わったほうがいいんじゃね？」と、日本社会に対してわりと本気で憂えています。
blocks.translation: Actually, regardless of creative work, I am fairly seriously concerned about Japanese society, thinking, “Isn’t it about time this upside-down society, where people prioritize work over their lives, came to an end?”

blocks.source: まあ、現実にはやむを得ないことがあるのも重々承知。それでも、せめて自分だけでもあがいてみるつもりです。
blocks.translation: Of course, I fully understand that there are things that cannot be helped in reality. Even so, I intend to struggle at least for my own sake.
